profile.reading:
CoreSite VA1 is the original building of CoreSite's three building Reston, Virginia campus, addressed at 12100 Sunrise Valley Drive per the operator's own facility page. The Reston campus, formerly known as Sunrise Technology Park, sits on a 21.73 acre tract in Fairfax County's Hunter Mill District. Fairfax County planning commission records show CoreSite Real Estate Sunrise Technology Park LLC brought rezoning case RZ 2017-HM-032 and special exception case SE 2017-HM-030 before the Planning Commission on June 28, 2018, where all three related motions carried unanimously 10 to 0 with two commissioners recused, covering tax map parcels 17-3((1))17B, 23, and 32A. The Fairfax County Board of Supervisors gave final approval on July 31, 2018, which the county's own public affairs office described at the time as the first approval under new county land use provisions meant to more easily allow data centers to locate in Fairfax County. The approved plan converted roughly 463,212 square feet of 1980s office buildings, the site having previously been an AOL office campus that Boston Properties sold in 2016 for 60 million dollars, into a buildout eventually totaling more than 943,600 square feet across six buildings of two to four stories, carried out in four phases with the first phase already underway at approval. The case raised the site's floor area ratio from 0.5 to 0.99 and required LEED Silver certification for all buildings on the property.

CoreSite's own current facility page for VA1 states more than 261,000 square feet for this specific building, though the operator's separate spec sheet landing page instead cites a forward looking full build out figure of more than 1.3 million square feet for the whole campus and, elsewhere on that same page, a present day campus total of over 986,000 square feet, two campus wide figures from the same operator that do not reconcile with each other. No megawatt capacity or opening year specific to VA1 is published by CoreSite, and the operator states only N plus 2 generator redundancy at the campus level rather than a building specific standby generation figure, so none of the four power numbers this registry tracks are asserted for VA1. CoreSite lists SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA compliance across its facilities generally, without specifying which certifications apply building by building.

Fairfax County's tax department sought tenant identity and contact information for what a March 2024 filing described as CoreSite's four data centers and an office building at this same 12100 Sunrise Valley Drive address, and CoreSite responded by suing the county on March 8, 2024, arguing per Data Center Dynamics that not all tenants were county or state taxpayers, that some tenant contracts carried confidentiality obligations, and that the county's request was unduly burdensome. The county cited a Virginia Code provision allowing tax commissioners to require taxpayers to furnish tangible and intangible property information. No court ruling on that suit had been reported as of the source consulted. Separately, in November 2026 the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates creating a GS-5 data center rate class effective January 1, 2027, requiring 14 year mandatory contracts for facilities with 25 megawatts or more of demand, per Inside Climate News, a policy shift that will bear on this campus's future power arrangements regardless of VA1's own unpublished load. Parent company American Tower reported record CoreSite leasing driving stronger than expected second quarter 2026 results and budgeted roughly 695 million dollars in data center development spending for 2026 across CoreSite's markets, funding continued build out here among other campuses.

profile.capacity_note: not published by the operator at the building level. No reliable MW or power figure found in any aggregator source checked this session either.
profile.research_note: Gap-view review: no MW capacity figure is published by CoreSite for VA1 specifically. CoreSite's own pages give two conflicting Reston campus-wide totals (986,000 sqft "today" vs 1.3M+ sqft "at full build out"), neither of which is applied to this building. No power figure written.
sources_tried: CoreSites own Northern Virginia regional page and dedicated VA1 spec sheet page, plus a DataCenterMap aggregator listing found to be internally inconsistent on square footage and therefore not relied upon
profile.community_note: No organized resident opposition specific to VA1 was found in this research, in contrast to the newer V3 phase at 12367 Sunrise Valley Drive on the same broader campus, where FFXnow reported nearby Cocquina Cluster homeowners raising height, noise, traffic, light, and cooling tower steam concerns in 2025.
profile.square_footage: 261,000+ sq ft (operator figure). A third-party aggregator shows two mutually inconsistent figures for the same address, 201,000 and 188,000 sq ft, neither trusted over the operators own number.
profile.regulatory_note: Fairfax County approved the whole Reston campus, VA1 included, under rezoning case RZ 2017-HM-032 and special exception SE 2017-HM-030 on July 31, 2018, described by the county as its first approval under new provisions favoring data centers. Fairfax County's tax department separately sought tenant identity information covering this address in 2024, prompting a CoreSite lawsuit against the county filed March 8, 2024, unresolved as of the report reviewed. More restrictive countywide data center zoning standards the Board directed staff to draft on March 19, 2024 do not apply retroactively to this already approved campus.

reading.body:
CoreSite VA1 is a 261,000 square foot data center building at 12100 Sunrise Valley Drive in Reston, Virginia, part of a three-building campus on a 21.73 acre site approved for conversion from AOL office space under Fairfax County's first data center rezoning in July 2018. The operator publishes no megawatt capacity or power figure for this building. Without a stated load, the campus cannot be ranked among Virginia's published capacity facilities, though CoreSite reports record leasing across the Reston campus and parent company American Tower budgeted 695 million dollars in data center development spending for 2026 across CoreSite's markets.

The campus holds SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA certifications at the operator level, qualifying it to serve regulated workloads in finance, healthcare, and government without building-specific assertions. CoreSite operates the campus under N plus 2 generator redundancy at the campus level. Virginia's State Corporation Commission approved a new Dominion Energy data center rate class effective January 1, 2027, requiring 14 year power contracts for facilities drawing 25 megawatts or more, a policy that will apply here if VA1's load reaches that threshold, though the operator has not published whether it does.

CoreSite sued Fairfax County in March 2024 after the county's tax department sought tenant identity and contact information for the facility, arguing some contracts carry confidentiality obligations. The suit remained unresolved as of the source reviewed. No organized resident opposition specific to VA1 was reported, in contrast to nearby phases of the same campus where Cocquina Cluster homeowners raised height, noise, traffic, light, and cooling tower concerns in 2025.
